_readme: Copy this file to content/{id}.json and delete the _readme keys. See _SCHEMA.md. Validate with: python tools/validate_content.py
name: Example Subject
blurb: One sentence shown on the map card.

floors.title: Floor Title
floors.goal: One sentence: what the learner can do after finishing this floor.

lesson.title: Lesson Title
lesson.intro: Optional short paragraph setting up the floor. Delete if unused.

sections.title: First Idea
sections.body:
Explain one idea. Supports **bold**, `inline code`, blank-line paragraphs, and

- bullet lists
- like this
sections.code:
print("this runs in the browser")
print(2 + 3)

annotations.text: Annotate only the lines that carry the idea.

sections.title: Second Idea
sections.body: 2 to 4 sections per lesson. One idea each.

annotations.text: Line numbers are 1-based against this code block.

practice._readme: 6 to 10 practice challenges. All must pass to unlock the exam.
practice.prompt: State the task precisely. If output is checked, show it verbatim: `Hello!`
practice.starter: # starter code sets the shape, never the answer
practice.hint: Nudges toward the idea without giving the answer.

practice.prompt: An `expr` test checks a value instead of output. It works on bare variables too, so it is usable before functions are taught.
Write a function `add(a, b)` that returns the sum.
practice.solution:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

practice.prompt: `stdin` feeds lines to `input()`. One array element per line read.
Ships broken starter code. Otherwise identical to `code`.
The last practice challenge should combine every idea on the floor.

exam._readme: 8 to 12 exam challenges. 80% or better unlocks the next floor.
exam.prompt: Use MCQ only where code cannot test the idea.
exam.code: optional snippet shown above the choices — delete this key if unused
exam.explain: Shown after answering, whether right or wrong.
The engine really executes this and compares against the learner's answer.

exam.prompt: This should print `7` but it crashes. Fix it.
Exams mix all four kinds. Keep at least half of them code-writing.
